There are two curved isotherms in the figure, labeled 2℃ and 4℃ respectively on the right, and point P is between the 2℃ isotherm and the 4℃ isotherm. Then reason: the prompt states that this is an isotherm distribution map of a certain region in January, so the January temperature of the area where point P is located is roughly between 2℃ and 4℃. If considering China's coastal areas, the Pearl River Delta is farther south, but its January temperature is obviously higher than 4℃, which does not match the temperature range of point P in the figure; coastal areas farther north may have temperatures that match or are lower, but they are not the “southernmost.” A January temperature of about 2℃—4℃ and the southernmost possible corresponding area among coastal regions is the Yangtze River Delta.
